 J U D G M E N T

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .30,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Mr.P.Surendra S/o.Pasupuleti Vemula Naidu, in road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief:-
On 13.10.2024 at about 06.30 p.m., the deceased was proceeding on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA- 34-EE-5526, as a pillion rider, on extreme left side of road and when he reached Gulapalyam Railway Station Cross, on Guntakal to Uravakonda SH Road, Vajrakrur, Ananthapur District, a Car bearing Regn.No.AP-39-NT-6740,
driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner,
dashed to the motor cycle.

Due to the accident, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter he was shifted to Sunlife Hospital for treatment and then referred to Srinivas Hospital, wherein he succumbed to the injuries during the course of treatment.

Further the body was shifted to Ananthpur Government Hospital, wherein postmortem was conducted and body was handed over to petitioners and they have shifted the body to their native place and have spent a sum of .60,00,000/- towards funeral, obsequies ceremonies and towards the transportation of dead body.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was a Student and was also helping his father in Agricultural Operations.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners lost bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.
The respondents, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

sentences.text: 3. In pursuance of service of notice, 1st respondent appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.

The respondent No.2 did not appear before the tribunal and hence,
he has been placed ex-parte.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.1 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.1 has also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.1 has contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further contended that the car was not all involved in the alleged accident.
The rider of motor cycle was solely responsible for the alleged accident and the deceased was not wearing helmet also as on the date of accident.
Further contended that the driver of car was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Mr.P.Surendra succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 13.10.2024 at about 06.30 p.m., on Guntakal to Uravakonda SH Road, at Gulapalyam Railway Station Cross, Vajrakrur,
Ananthapur District, when deceased was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-34-EE-5526, as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.AP-39-NT-6740 by its driver?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to substantiate the contention of the petition, the Petitioner No.1/mother of deceased got examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed evidence of petitioners' side.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard arguments on both side and perused the materials available on records.
8.

This Tribunal answers the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per final order,
 for the following:

sentences.text: Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioners that deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 13.10.2024 at about 06.30 p.m., on Guntakal to Uravakonda SH Road, at Gulapalyam Railway Station Cross, Vajrakrur, Ananthapur District, when deceased was proceeding, as a pillion rider, on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-34-EE-5526, due to the rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.AP-39-NT-6740 by its driver, as a result he succumbed to injuries.
10. The Petitioner No.1/mother of deceased Mr.P.Surendra examined as PW.1.
In the chief- examination, PW.1 deposed that her son was proceeding on a motor cycle, due to the rash and negligent driving of car by its driver, the accident occurred.

In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of car, the petitioners produced Ex.P.2 First Information statement lodged by mother of deceased by name Smt.P.Poornima W/o.Vemula Naidu with police on 14.10.2024 pertaining to the accident occurred on 13.10.2024.
On the basis of first information lodged by mother of deceased, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable under section 125(a) BNS of M.V.Act.
In first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.
The FIR is registered against the driver of offending vehicle which does not appear to have been questioned either by driver or owner of offending vehicle.
11. The petitioners also furnished Spot Sketch and its translated version which are marked as Ex.P.3 & 3(a).
The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said documents.
Ex . P.4 - IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to vehicle are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of damages being caused to the offending vehicle.
The vehicle will be inspected after seizure of the same by the police.
The said document indicates the aspect of seizure of offending vehicle by the police on the ground of its involvement in the accident.
Respondent No.2 does not appear to have questioned the seizure procedure conducted by the police.
The IMV report discloses the aspect of offending vehicle being damaged.
The respondent No.2 not provided explanation regarding the manner in which the vehicle got damaged, if the same has not been involved in the accident.
Respondent No.2 could have provided proper explanation pertaining to the manner in which the vehicle got damaged, if the same has not been involved in the accident.
The IMV report indicates the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. Ex.P.5 & 5(a) is the Inquest Report and its translated version.
Ex.P.6 is the PM report, wherein deceased Mr.Pasupuleti Surendra S/o.P.Vemula Naidu is stated to have died due to Craniocerebral injuries sustained.
The I.O., after detailed investigation filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.134/2024 U/s.106(1) of BNS of Vajrakarur PS as per Ex.P.7.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.
The documents furnished by petitioners disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of car in the cause of accident.

The respondents not placed any materials in order to rebut or disprove the documents furnished by the petitioners related to the Pasupuleti Purnima vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28755393/

sentences.text: The owner or driver of the car does not appear to have challenged the FIR as well as final report filed by the police against the driver of offending vehicle.
The correctness of investigation does not appear to have been challenged by respondents in any manner.
In the cross examination of PW.1 also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited from the witness.
13. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioners.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be looked into in order to ascertain the aspect of negligence.
The materials placed before the Tribunal points towards the negligence on the part of driver of offending car in the cause of accident.
So, the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners discloses that the accident was caused due to rash and negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of petitioners coupled with the documents produced before this tribunal, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.AP-39-NT-6740 by its driver and deceased succumbed to injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

14. Issue No.2:- While discussing the issue No.1 this tribunal has observed that the petitioners have proved that Mr.P.Surendra, S/o.Pasupuleti Vemula Naidu died in a road accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the car by its driver.
Thus, the records and the oral evidence produced by the petitioners are sufficient to prove that petitioners are the grand parents of deceased Mr.P.Surendra.
They are entitled for compensation for the death of Mr.P.Surendra in a road accident.

15. The petitioners contended that petitioner No.1 is the mother, petitioner No.2 is the brother and petitioner No.3 and 4 are the Grand parents of deceased Mr.P.Surendra and contended that the deceased was aged about 14 years at the time of accident.
In order to prove the age of deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.11 Notarized Copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein the date of birth of deceased is mentioned as 25.02.2012.
The accident occurred on 13.10.2024.
As per the document furnished by petitioners, the age of the deceased appears to be 13 years at the time of accident.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to dispute or rebut the document furnished by petitioners related to the age of deceased.

In the absence of materials to the contrary,
the document furnished by petitioners is to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
As per the materials furnished before the Tribunal, the age of deceased was 13 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
According to the petition and the evidence of PW.1 deceased was 13 years and he was a student.
The petitioners have claimed .30,00,000/- as compensation towards loss of future earnings, love and affection and loss of estate, funeral expenses.
16. Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioners contended that the deceased took treatment at the Hospital.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.9 - Discharge Summary, which reveals that her son took treatment in Sreenivasa Hospital, wherein he took treatment from 13.10.2024 to 16.10.2024 i.e., for a period of three days.
The petitioner has also produced medical bills for a sum of .73,477/- marked at Ex.P.8.

sentences.text: 19. This Tribunal has carefully perused the decisions relied by counsel for petitioners and respondent No.1.

In the decision relied by counsel for petitioners which is mentioned at serial No.3 above, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has considered the decisions relied by counsel for respondent No.1 and by applying the principle laid down in Hitesh Nagjibhai Patel's case, held that the income of deceased must be calculated based on the provisions of Minimum Wages Act.

As such,
the decisions relied by counsel for respondent No.1 is not applicable to the case on hand.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has relied on the decision of Hon'ble Apex court in Civil Appeal No.10278/2025 between Hitesh Nagjibhai Patel Vs Bababhai Nagjibhai Rabari and another for calculating the income of deceased and held that the income has to be calculated based on the provisions of Minimum Wages Act.

On consideration of materials on record and the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in above mentioned decision, the income of deceased minor is considered as .15,000/- per month and 40% is added towards future prospects.
Thus, the income of deceased is considered as .21,000/- (.15,000/- + .6,000/-).
Further, as the income of deceased minor has been considered on per with the income of a major, 50% of the income is deducted towards his personal expenses.
Hence, the income of deceased is considered as .10,500/-.

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of .21,39,477/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakhs Thirty Nine Thousand Four Hundred and Seventy Seven only)
with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 being the wife of deceased is entitled for 40%, petitioner No.2 is minor son is entitled for 20% and petitioner No.3 & 4 being the parents of deceased are entitled for 20% each of the compensation amount.
In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.1, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1, and 40% of the amount shall be kept in FD.

20% each of compensation amount allotted to the share of minor petitioner No.2 shall be kept in FD in his name of minor petitioner in any of the Nationalized Bank or Scheduled Bank of the choice of minor guardian for a period of 3 years or till he attains the age of majority whichever is later.
The guardian of petitioner is entitled for interest that accrues on FD periodically.
In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.3 & 4, entire amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.3 & 4 as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioners hereby directed to produce particulars of Bank Account of petitioners, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioners, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioners shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioners are entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Office to draw Award accordingly.
